headline: This law lets the National Native American Veterans' Memorial be built on National Mall land and changes who selects its design and pays for it.
what_it_does: The law amends the 1994 act that created the National Native American Veterans' Memorial. It allows the memorial to be built on property under the National Museum of the American Indian on the National Mall, instead of only inside the Museum building. It lets the Museum take part in choosing the design, with more say than a consultative role, alongside the National Congress of American Indians. The Museum and the Congress now share responsibility for accepting donations and paying the memorial's costs, which previously fell only to the Congress.
when_it_takes_effect: The official summary does not give a specific effective date. It was enacted on December 26, 2013.
